The AI Builder is the **primary way customers extend ObjectOS**. Open
ObjectOS, describe what you need in plain language, and it builds the
metadata for you — objects, fields, views, dashboards, flows, whole apps.
Nothing is built until you approve the plan, and everything it builds is
ordinary ObjectStack metadata you can read, change and package.

## Two agents: the Builder and the Assistant

ObjectOS ships two AI agents. You do not choose between them: **where you
ask** decides which one answers.

| | **Builder** (`build`) | **Assistant** (`ask`) |
|---|---|---|
| Where | The AI Builder, in the app-building surface | The chat in the data console, beside your records |
| What it does | Designs and changes the **app**: objects, fields, views, dashboards, flows | Answers questions about your **data**, draws charts, and runs the actions your app exposes |
| What it never does | — | Change the application. A build request that reaches it is declined and pointed to the Builder, never silently re-routed |

Both run **as the signed-in person**. Every tool call is checked against that
person's permissions, record access and field-level security, so the AI can
never see or change more than they could themselves.

**Who can use the Builder.** An AI seat alone is not enough: the Builder changes
your app's metadata, so it also needs the `manage_metadata` or `studio.access`
permission. A member without either sees only the Assistant, a direct request
to the Builder is refused with `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, and every build tool
checks the permission again when it runs.

## Try it

```
You: I need to track customer support tickets.
     Each ticket has a subject, description, priority (low/medium/high/urgent),
     status (new/open/pending/resolved/closed), and assignee.

AI:  Here's the plan:
     • Object `support_ticket` with 5 fields
     • A kanban view grouped by status
     • A dashboard of open tickets by priority
     • A few sample tickets to try it with

     Shall I build it?

You: Yes

AI:  ✓ Object created
     ✓ Kanban view and dashboard created
     ✓ Sample data added
     Published — open Support Tickets to try it.
```

You now have a working ticketing app — REST endpoints, generated views,
audit log entries, permission checkpoints, the works. No file was
edited; no restart happened.

## How a build runs

1. **Plan.** For anything larger than a single change — "build me a recruiting
   system" — the Builder first proposes a **blueprint**: the objects, fields,
   relationships, views, dashboards and sample data it intends to create, with
   its assumptions. Nothing is created at this step.
2. **Approve.** You answer in the chat: approve it, or ask for changes and get a
   revised plan. The Builder makes changes only after you approve them in that
   conversation.
3. **Build as drafts.** The approved changes are written as **drafts** — staged,
   not yet live.
4. **Verify.** The Builder checks the drafts against the platform's rules and
   fixes what it can before anything goes live.
5. **Publish.** The drafts are published into the environment you are building
   in, and the app appears there with its sample data. A status panel shows
   what has actually been published; the Builder never reports a change as
   shipped when it is not.

To extend an existing app, say so — *"add a satisfaction survey to the support
app"* — and the Builder designs the new pieces to link to that app's objects and
adds them to its navigation, instead of building a separate app.

## What you can ask for

| Goal | Prompt |
|---|---|
| New object | *"Create a `product` object with name, sku, price, category."* |
| Add field | *"Add a `discount` decimal field to `order`, max 50."* |
| Picklist change | *"On `task.status`, add 'blocked' between 'open' and 'done'."* |
| Relationship | *"Make `order_line` master-detail to `order`."* |
| Validation | *"On `invoice`, the discount can't exceed the subtotal."* |
| Flow | *"When a high-priority ticket sits in 'new' for 30 minutes, notify the manager."* |
| Action | *"Create an action `approve_invoice` that sets status to approved."* |
| Permission set | *"Create `agent` permission set with read/create/edit on support_ticket and read on customer."* |
| Translation | *"Translate the support_ticket labels and picklists to Spanish."* |

If the AI can't do it, it says so — and points you at the manual path.

## The tools the agents call

An agent's abilities are its tools. See the live catalog for an environment
at `GET /api/v1/ai/tools`.

**The Builder's authoring tools** work on [packages](/docs/build/packages) and
their metadata, and are validated against `@objectstack/spec`:

| Area | Tools |
|---|---|
| Plans | `propose_blueprint`, `apply_blueprint` |
| Packages | `create_package`, `list_packages`, `get_package`, `get_active_package`, `set_active_package` |
| Objects | `create_object`, `list_objects`, `describe_object` |
| Fields | `add_field`, `modify_field`, `delete_field` |

**The Assistant's data tools** read and act on records:

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `query_records` | Query an object with filters, field selection, sort and paging. Each record comes back with its `id`, so an answer can link the records it names. |
| `get_record` | Fetch one record by id. |
| `aggregate_data` | Server-side `count`, `sum`, `avg`, `min`, `max` and `count_distinct`, optionally grouped and filtered. |
| `query_data` | Answer a plain-language request: it finds the relevant object, writes the query, runs it and returns the records. |
| `visualize_data` | The one tool that draws a chart: it aggregates an object by a dimension over one or more measures and draws a bar, column, horizontal-bar, line, area, pie, donut, radar or scatter chart in the chat. The axis shows display values — option labels, record names — in the chat's language. Needs the environment's analytics service. |
| `search_knowledge` | Search your registered knowledge sources (record snapshots, files, URLs). Results are already filtered to what the person may see. Present when a knowledge service is set up. |
| `action_<name>` | Run one of your app's business actions, exposed to AI (below). |

`aggregate_data` is part of the in-product AI. An agent connected from outside
over [MCP](/docs/configure/mcp) gets its own tool set, described there.

## Actions as tools

An action becomes a tool named `action_<name>` when its author **exposes it to
AI** — `ai: { exposed: true }` with an `ai.description` of at least 40
characters, on a type that runs without a UI (`script`, `flow` or `api`).
Once exposed, the AI can call it like any built-in tool, under the caller's
permissions; an action that is not exposed never becomes one. See
[Actions](/docs/build/interface/actions#from-an-ai-agent).

**Approval before an action runs.** An action that declares
`ai.requiresConfirmation: true` — or looks destructive without declaring
otherwise — is not run straight away. The AI files it as a **pending action**,
and it runs only when approved:

| Endpoint | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `GET  /api/v1/ai/pending-actions` | List your pending actions (filter by status) |
| `GET  /api/v1/ai/pending-actions/:id` | One of your pending actions |
| `POST /api/v1/ai/pending-actions/:id/approve` | Approve and run it |
| `POST /api/v1/ai/pending-actions/:id/reject` | Reject it, with an optional reason |

A pending action belongs to the person whose conversation proposed it: only
they can read, approve or reject it. Anyone else, an administrator included,
is answered as if it did not exist.

## Chatting through the API

Send a conversation to an agent by name, `ask` or `build`:

```bash
curl -X POST https://your-environment-host/api/v1/ai/agents/ask/chat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "messages": [{ "role": "user", "content": "How many open opportunities over $50k?" }],
    "context": { "appName": "crm", "objectName": "opportunity" }
  }'
```

- **`messages`** — the conversation so far. Only `user` and `assistant` turns
  are accepted from the client.
- **`context`** — where the person is: `appName`, `objectName`, `viewName`,
  `recordId`. Skills use it to decide what is relevant.
- **`conversationId`** (optional) — continue an existing conversation.

Answers **stream** by default as Server-Sent Events (the Vercel AI data stream
protocol, `x-vercel-ai-ui-message-stream: v1`); charts arrive in the stream as
`data-chart` parts. Send `"stream": false` for a single JSON answer instead.

Conversations are kept under `/api/v1/ai/conversations`, and each person sees
only their own.

## Limits

- **Data access follows the person's own permissions**, for reading and for
  actions alike.
- **System packages are off limits.** Asking the AI to change a system package
  (`sys_*`) is refused.
- **Large builds go better in steps.** "Build a full HR app" works, but a
  series of smaller conversations, each landing one area, is easier to review.
- **On ObjectOS Cloud**, the AI draws on the environment's
  [AI allowance](/docs/cloud/ai-credits-and-limits), and an environment holds at
  most 500 unpublished drafts ([Storage and Limits](/docs/cloud/storage-and-limits#drafts-and-authoring-writes)).
  On a self-managed Enterprise deployment the model is your own, configured in
  [AI Service](/docs/configure/ai).

## Going beyond build-time AI

The same AI plumbing powers **runtime agents** for your end users —
support assistants, sales co-pilots, internal Q&A bots — built on
the same Agent → Skill → Tool architecture. See [Agents](/docs/build/agents).
